chunks.text: Dairy goat breeds commonly kept in Tanzania include Toggenburg (daily milk yield 1.5-2.5 litres, lactation 250-300 days), Alpine (1.5-3.0 litres, hardy and adaptable), Saanen (2.0-4.0 litres, highest yield but heat sensitive), and Nubian (1.0-2.0 litres, high butterfat milk). Boer goats are raised for meat production (mature buck 80-120 kg, doe 60-80 kg, kid growth rate 150-250 grams/day). East African local goats are hardy and disease resistant but yield only 0.5-1.0 litres milk per day.

Vaccination schedule for goats in Tanzania: Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) — vaccine: Multivax P (Merial), 2ml SC, vaccinate at 4 months then every 6 months. Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia (CCPP) — vaccine: CCPP vaccine (KEVEVAPI), 1ml SC, vaccinate at 3-6 months then annually. Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) — vaccine: PPR vaccine (KEVEVAPI), 1ml SC, vaccinate at 3-4 months then every 3 years. Anthrax — vaccine: Sterne spore vaccine, 0.5ml SC, annual booster. Blackleg — vaccine: Multivax P, 2ml SC, annual. Tetanus — vaccine: Tetanus toxoid, 1ml SC, annual. Enterotoxaemia (Clostridium perfringens C+D) — vaccine: Multivax P or Ovilis C+D, 2ml SC, vaccinate kids at 8 weeks then booster at 12 weeks, then annually.

Deworming protocols for goats: Anthelmintic classes available in Tanzania: Benzimidazoles (Albendazole 10mg/kg oral, Fenbendazole 10mg/kg oral), Macrocyclic lactones (Ivermectin 0.2mg/kg SC, 0.2mg/kg pour-on), Imidazothiazoles (Levamisole 8mg/kg oral, 7.5mg/kg SC). Rotate between drug classes every 3-4 treatments to prevent resistance. FAMACHA scoring: Score 1 (red) — no treatment, Score 2 (red-pink) — monitor, Score 3 (pink) — treat if other signs, Score 4 (pink-white) — treat, Score 5 (white) — treat urgently. Targeted selective treatment: only treat animals with FAMACHA 3-5, body condition <2.5, or faecal egg count >2000 epg.

Bloat in goats: Frothy bloat — caused by rapid fermentation of legume pastures (lucerne, clover). Signs: sudden distension of left flank, distress, difficulty breathing. Treatment: administer 50-100ml vegetable oil orally (anti-foaming agent), trocarize if severe (14-gauge needle left flank), walk animal. Free gas bloat — caused by obstruction of oesophageal groove. Treatment: pass stomach tube to relieve gas. Prevention: avoid turning hungry goats onto lush legume pasture, provide hay before legume grazing.

Mastitis in goats: Clinical signs: swollen, hot, painful udder; clotted or watery milk; reduced milk yield; sometimes systemic fever. Subclinical: no visible signs, elevated somatic cell count. Treatment: intramammary infusion of antibiotics (e.g., Teramycin intramammary, one tube per affected half, repeat in 12 hours). Supportive: strip udder frequently, hot compresses, NSAID for pain. Prevention: proper milking hygiene, teat dipping with iodine-based dip (0.5% available iodine), dry doe treatment with long-acting intramammary antibiotic at drying off.

Pneumonia in goats: Causes: stress (transport, overcrowding, weather change), viral (PPRV, CAEV) and bacterial (Mannheimia haemolytica, Pasteurella multocida) agents. Signs: nasal discharge, coughing, rapid breathing, fever >40.5°C, depression, reduced appetite. Treatment: Oxytetracycline LA 20mg/kg IM for 3-5 days, or Enrofloxacin 5mg/kg SC for 3-5 days. Supportive: keep warm, ensure hydration, isolate. Prevention: adequate ventilation, avoid overcrowding, vaccinate against PPR and CCPP.

Footrot in goats: Caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum and Dichelobacter nodosus in wet conditions. Signs: lameness, foul-smelling discharge between claws, separation of hoof wall. Treatment: foot trimming to remove infected tissue, footbath in 10% zinc sulphate or 10% copper sulphate for 30 minutes, systemic antibiotics (Oxytetracycline LA 20mg/kg IM for 5 days). Severe cases: Procaine penicillin 22,000 IU/kg IM for 5 days. Prevention: avoid wet muddy conditions, regular foot trimming, quarantine new animals, footbath after rain.

Kid management protocol: Colostrum: first feed within 2 hours of birth, minimum 10% body weight in first 24 hours (e.g., 400ml for 4kg kid). Quality assessment: colostrometer or check that it is thick and yellow. If dam cannot feed: frozen colostrum thawed at <50°C, or artificial colostrum (1 litre warm milk + 1 egg yolk + 1 teaspoon cod liver oil + 1 teaspoon castor oil). Navel dipping: 7% iodine solution within 30 minutes of birth. Disbudding: at 7-10 days using hot iron or caustic paste, with pain management. Creep feeding: introduce from 2 weeks, high protein (18% CP) creep ration. Weaning: at 90 days or 12kg body weight.

Reproduction in goats: Oestrus cycle length: 21 days (range 18-24). Oestrus duration: 24-48 hours. Signs of heat: tail flagging, mucous discharge, vocalisation, standing to be mounted, swollen vulva, reduced appetite. Optimal mating: 12-18 hours after onset of heat. Gestation length: 150 days (range 145-155). Pre-kidding preparation: 7 days before due date move to kidding pen, check udder development, prepare kidding kit (iodine, towels, lubricant, gloves, scissors). Kidding: normal presentation is two front feet with head between them. Stage 1 (cervix dilation): 1-12 hours. Stage 2 (expulsion): 30 minutes to 2 hours. Stage 3 (placenta): 1-4 hours. Retained placenta after 12 hours requires veterinary attention.

Nutritional requirements for goats: Dry matter intake: 3-4% of body weight for adult does, 4-5% for growing kids. Lactating doe: 12-16% crude protein, 2.4-2.8 Mcal/kg metabolizable energy. Dry doe: 8-10% CP, 2.0-2.2 Mcal/kg ME. Growing kid: 14-16% CP, 2.6-2.8 Mcal/kg ME. Body condition scoring: 1 (very thin, spine sharp, ribs visible) to 5 (obese). Target BCS at mating: 2.5-3.0. Target BCS at kidding: 3.0-3.5. Common feeds in Tanzania: Napier grass (10-14% CP), Rhodes grass (8-10% CP), lucerne/alfalfa (16-20% CP), maize bran (9% CP), sunflower cake (30-35% CP), cotton seed cake (25-30% CP).
